title: Best Grill Mat Sizes for Small Patio Grills and Smokers
meta_description: Discover the best grill mat sizes for small patio grills. Learn how to measure, cut, and protect your delicate foods with our expert guide.
html:
Grilling on a small patio shouldn’t mean sacrificing functionality just because you’re tight on space. If you’ve ever lost a slice of zucchini through the grates of your portable hibachi or struggled with fish sticking to your apartment-size smoker, you know the struggle. Finding the best grill mat sizes for your specific setup is the game-changer you need to elevate those weeknight dinners. A good mat keeps your grill clean, prevents flare-ups in confined spaces, and ensures every piece of food makes it to the plate.

Assessing Your Grill’s Footprint

Before you buy, you need to look at your actual cooking surface, not just the overall dimensions of the grill. Small patio grills, like the Weber Q series or pellet grills such as the Traeger Tailgater, often have curved lids that hang lower than you expect. If you buy a mat that touches the lid, you risk melting the material or preventing proper ventilation.

Measure the grates themselves. For most small kettle grills or bullet smokers, the cooking grate is circular and often smaller than the diameter of the lid. You want a mat that covers as much of the usable area as possible without overlapping the edges. Overhanging mats can burn and curl, releasing fumes you don’t want in a small, enclosed patio area.

Standard Dimensions and the Best Grill Mat Sizes

While mats come in various shapes, most are sold in rectangular sheets because they are versatile. However, when dealing with small rigs, one size does not fit all. Here is a breakdown of the common sizes you will encounter and how they fit small gear:

  • 15.75 x 15.75 inches: This is the standard square size. It is excellent for small gas grills or square pellet grills. It offers substantial coverage but will need to be trimmed down for round kettle grills.
  • 13 x 15.75 inches: Slightly narrower, this size is perfect for rectangular portable grills or smaller charcoal baskets where width is limited.
  • 17 x 24 inches: Generally too large for a single small grill, but this can be cut in half to create two custom mats for smaller round surfaces.

When to Cut Your Mats to Size

One of the biggest advantages of grill mats is that they are customizable. If you are using a small circular charcoal grill, a large square mat creates wasted material and potential burn hazards where the corners hang off. Do not be afraid to trim your mats.

Use a sharp pair of household scissors to cut the mat to the exact shape of your grate. For round grills, place the mat on top, trace the edge with a marker (or eyeball it if you are confident), and cut. A critical tip for longevity: round the corners of your cut edges. Sharp 90-degree corners tend to peel and fray faster than rounded ones, especially when exposed to high heat in a small smoker.

Thickness and Heat Distribution

Size isn't the only factor; thickness plays a huge role in how the mat performs on smaller equipment. Small grills often have hot spots because the heat source is closer to the food. A mat that is too thin (often advertised as 0.1mm or less) might burn through quickly or warp.

Look for mats that are at least 0.2mm to 0.3mm thick. This heavier gauge material sits flatter on the grates and conducts heat more evenly, which is vital when you are cooking delicate foods on a high-heat portable propane grill. A thicker mat also lies heavier, preventing it from being blown around by the wind—a common issue on breezy patios.

Ideal for Sensitive Ingredients

Using a mat effectively changes your small grill into a flat-top griddle or a baking sheet. This is particularly useful for delicate items that would otherwise fall through the wider grates of economy grills. Whether you are searing scallops, cooking asparagus, or preparing sticky wings, the barrier keeps the food intact and the grill clean.

For those looking to maximize their setup, the BBQ Grill Mats offer a reliable solution. These reusable non-stick mats are specifically designed to grill delicate foods without flare-ups or sticking. Because they work with any grill type, they are versatile enough to switch between your gas grill on the patio and your electric smoker if the weather turns.

Cleaning and Storage for Small Spaces

Living in an apartment or condo often means your outdoor storage is limited. Grill mats are infinitely superior to foil or pans because they are reusable and flat. Once they cool down, a quick wipe with a damp cloth or a run through the dishwasher (top rack only) removes the grease.

Because they are thin, you can stack them in a drawer or hang them on a hook inside a cabinet. This ease of storage makes them a must-have accessory for the space-conscious griller who wants big flavor without the big cleanup.

FAQ

Can I use grill mats on a pellet grill or smoker?

Yes, but be mindful of airflow. On a pellet grill, place the mat on the grates but avoid covering the entire surface if your grill relies on specific airflow paths. On a smoker, mats are great for catching drips, but they may inhibit heavy smoke penetration if used for the entire duration of a low-and-slow cook.

Do grill mats affect the flavor of the food?

Grill mats do not significantly alter the flavor, but they do change the texture. You won't get direct sear marks through the mat, so the food will have a more even, pan-seared texture rather than a char-grilled look. However, you still get the smoke flavor from the grill.

At what temperature do grill mats melt?

Most high-quality grill mats are rated for temperatures up to 500°F or even 600°F. However, you should never place them directly over a direct open flame, such as the burner tubes of a gas grill. Place them over the grates where the heat is indirect and distributed.
